reason: Implement the body: compute and return what the name and the intent's expected output promise; a declared-but-unimplemented member (a reserved hook whose only meaning is 'not yet') raises NotImplementedError naming the missing piece — give the function an effect without inventing one (the owner's form, hand check #17, 2026-09-16).
before:
def reserved():
    """Reserved for a later release."""
rendering_rationale: shape `def <name>(<params>): """<existing docstring>""" raise NotImplementedError("<name>: not implemented")` — every placeholder is read straight off the function: `<name>`=reserved, `<params>`=none, the docstring is the one already there. A body that is only a docstring returns None silently; the raise makes the promise honest.

reason: Return on every path: give the missing branch / fall-through the value the annotation promises or raise the documented error; a function that may return nothing is annotated Optional and returns None explicitly.
rendering_rationale: shape `if <cond>: return <value>; return <value for the other case>`. The name fixes both missing values: `sign` is -1 / 0 / 1, and the annotation `-> int` says every path must return an int — the fall-through was None.

reason: Make the container instance-owned: assign a fresh list / dict / set in __init__ and mutate it through self; keep it at class level only when the intent says every instance shares it.
rendering_rationale: shape `def __init__(self, ...): self.<name> = []   # or {} / set()`. `<name>`=items and the container is a list — the class body's own `items = []` says so, and appending to that CLASS attribute is the infraction (every instance shares one list). The instance gets its own before the append.

reason: Assign the name before its first read: move the assignment above the read when the same value was meant, or initialise it (None / empty / the parameter) at the top of the function.
before:
def label_for(code):
    text = prefix + str(code)
    prefix = "C-"
    return text
after:
def label_for(code):
    prefix = "C-"
    text = prefix + str(code)
    return text
rendering_rationale: shape `<name> = <initial value>\n... <first read of <name>> ...`. `<name>`=prefix and `<initial value>`="C-", both already in the function — the only defect is the order: the read stood above the binding, so the function raised UnboundLocalError on every call.

reason: Give the function its effect: return the value or perform the action the name and the intent promise (a write, a call, a state change) and make the caller use it.
rendering_rationale: shape `def <name>(...): <action | return <value>>`. `value.strip` named the method and never called it, so nothing happened and nothing was returned; the two readings the shape offers collapse into one here — call it and return the result.

reason: Remove the bidi control characters and write the visible text the string is meant to carry; a right-to-left segment, if intended, is marked in data, not with control characters in source.
rendering_rationale: shape `<NAME> = '<the intended visible text — no U+202A..U+202E / U+2066..U+2069 controls>'`. The literal held U+202E (RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE) between `total ` and `latot`, which renders as a second `total`. The intended visible text is therefore `total total`, written with no control characters.

reason: Rename the method to a plain name (serialize, validate) and call it explicitly, or implement the real protocol hook Python calls (__repr__, __iter__, __eq__ …) when that is what was meant.
rendering_rationale: shape `def <plain_name>(self, ...):   # was __<name>__`. `<plain_name>`=serialize: `__serialize__` invents a dunder Python's data model does not define, so nothing ever calls it implicitly. The body is honest and is kept; the only call site in the file is the def itself, so the rename reaches everything.
